Description: Offer 15-20% discount for annual prepayment. Improves cash flow, reduces churn (commitment), increases LTV.
When_To_Use: After validating monthly pricing|When cash flow is priority|When churn is >5%/month
How_To_Do: Offer 2 months free on annual (=17% discount)|Default to annual on pricing page|Show monthly as 'per month billed annually'|Add toggle with savings highlighted
Expected_Impact: 20-30% of customers switch to annual. Churn drops 5-10%. Cash flow improves immediately.
Anti_Pattern: More than 25% discount (signals desperation)|Forcing annual only (some customers need monthly)

Description: Grow revenue from existing customers through usage upgrades, seat additions, plan upgrades. Target NRR >110%.
When_To_Use: When you have tiered plans|When usage naturally grows|When CAC is high (cheaper to expand than acquire)
How_To_Do: Add usage-based component to subscription|Create clear upgrade triggers (hitting limits)|Proactive outreach at 80% usage|Cross-sell complementary features
Expected_Impact: NRR >110% means you grow even with some churn. Best-in-class SaaS: 120-140% NRR.
Anti_Pattern: No upgrade path in product|Only relying on new acquisition|Price increases without added value

Description: 30-40% of churn is involuntary (failed payments). Recover with smart dunning: retry logic + email sequences + in-app notifications.
When_To_Use: When churn rate >3% monthly|When payment failure rate is visible in Stripe dashboard
How_To_Do: Smart retry timing (days 1, 3, 5, 7)|Pre-dunning email before expiry|In-app banner for failed payment|Easy card update flow (Stripe customer portal)|Grace period before cancellation
Expected_Impact: Recover 30-50% of failed payments. Can reduce overall churn by 1-2% points.
Anti_Pattern: Immediately canceling on first failure|No pre-dunning emails|Hard cancel without grace period|Not tracking involuntary vs voluntary churn

Description: Price based on the metric that correlates with customer value. Examples: messages sent, team members, API calls, revenue processed.
When_To_Use: When customers get different value from product|When usage varies significantly|When you want pricing to scale with customer success
How_To_Do: Identify your value metric (what correlates with 'aha moment')|Test 2-3 potential metrics|Implement metered billing|Set generous free tier|Make upgrade natural at success milestones
Expected_Impact: Revenue scales automatically with customer growth. Reduces friction at entry. Better LTV:CAC.
Anti_Pattern: Pricing on wrong metric (not aligned with value)|Too complex metering|No usage dashboard for customers|Surprise bills

Description: When raising prices: grandfather existing customers at old price (6-12 months) then migrate gradually. Prevents mass churn from price changes.
When_To_Use: When implementing price increase|When changing pricing model|When adding new tiers
How_To_Do: Announce 60+ days before change|Grandfather for 6-12 months|Offer migration incentive (extra features)|Personal outreach to top 20% accounts|Track churn during transition
Expected_Impact: Retain 85-95% of existing customers through price change. Signal: you value loyalty.
Anti_Pattern: Surprise price increases|No grandfathering period|Generic mass email|No opt-in to new pricing benefits

Description: Optimize free-to-paid conversion. Industry average: 2-5%. Top performers: 8-15%. Key: right paywall placement + activation triggers.
When_To_Use: When conversion rate <5%|When free users aren't upgrading|When you have freemium model
How_To_Do: Map activation milestones (what free users do before converting)|Place paywall AFTER value demonstrated|Show 'what you're missing' teasers|Time-limited feature previews|Remove friction from upgrade flow
Expected_Impact: Double conversion rate from freemium baseline. Each 1% improvement = significant MRR growth.
Anti_Pattern: Paywall too early (before value)|Too generous free tier (no reason to upgrade)|No activation tracking|Upgrade flow requires sales call

Description: Growth Rate % + Profit Margin % should exceed 40. Balances growth with profitability. <40 = unhealthy. >40 = excellent. Bootstrap target: 30+.
When_To_Use: Quarterly financial health check|Before fundraising|When deciding growth vs profitability trade-off
How_To_Do: Calculate: (MRR growth rate %) + (net profit margin %)|If <40: either grow faster OR improve margins|Bootstrap: aim for >30 initially|Track monthly trend
Expected_Impact: Benchmark for investors and self-assessment. Companies above 40 valued at 2-3x premium.
Anti_Pattern: Only optimizing one side (growth OR profit)|Ignoring until fundraising|Comparing to companies in different stage

Description: Don't rely on single revenue stream. Combine: SaaS subscription + one-time purchases (templates/tools) + services (consulting/setup).
When_To_Use: When primary revenue is fragile|When you have expertise to productize|When customers ask for services alongside product
How_To_Do: Start with primary SaaS|Add template/resource marketplace|Offer premium onboarding service|Consider affiliate revenue|Add API access tier for developers
Expected_Impact: 30-40% more stable revenue. Reduces risk from single-product dependency.
Anti_Pattern: Too many streams too early (focus!)|Services that don't scale|Revenue streams that cannibalize each other
